original_text: The well-known Borde-Guth-Vilenkin Theorem shows that inflationary spacetimes are generically geodesically past-incomplete, necessitating the existence of a pre-inflationary boundary of some sort, possibly singular.
injected_text: The well-known Borde-Guth-Vilenkin Theorem shows that all expanding spacetimes are generically geodesically past-incomplete, necessitating the existence of a pre-inflationary boundary of some sort, possibly singular.
rationale: The cited Borde-Guth-Vilenkin paper explicitly conditions its past-incompleteness conclusion on inflationary spacetimes (those with positive average expansion rate H_av along a past-directed geodesic); replacing 'inflationary' with the broader 'all expanding' drops that scope qualifier and over-generalises to spacetimes such as loitering / asymptotically-Minkowski models which are expanding but past-complete, while leaving the cite key, the directional claim, and the methodological language (BGV theorem, past-incompleteness) untouched.
ground_truth_description: In the abstract, the scope qualifier 'inflationary' attached to the BGV-theorem statement was replaced with 'all expanding', over-generalising the cited claim to spacetimes for which Borde-Guth-Vilenkin do not establish past-incompleteness.

truth.claim_sentence_verbatim: The well-known Borde-Guth-Vilenkin Theorem shows that inflationary spacetimes are generically geodesically past-incomplete, necessitating the existence of a pre-inflationary boundary of some sort, possibly singular.
